On the Mac, a left click on the menu-bar icon opens the web app and a right click opens the menu, like on Windows. Both apps can now leave the task running when a check-in goes unanswered.

## Download

- **macOS 13 or newer** (Apple Silicon and Intel): [TasksBar.zip](https://github.com/Astervista/tasks/releases/download/v3.1.0/TasksBar.zip)
- **Windows** (64-bit): [TasksTray.exe](https://github.com/Astervista/tasks/releases/download/v3.1.0/TasksTray.exe)

The apps aren't signed yet, so your system will warn you the first time:

- **macOS:** unzip, move `TasksBar.app` to Applications (replacing the old one), then run this once:
  ```sh
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/TasksBar.app
  ```
- **Windows:** choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

## What's new

- **Clicks on the Mac like on Windows:** a left click on the menu-bar icon opens the web app next to it, and another closes it. A right click (or Control-click) opens the menu.
- **Pause unanswered check-ins:** a new item in the menu of both apps, on by default. Turned off, the "how far along?" question waits for your answer and the task keeps running, instead of being paused after 10 minutes. It's saved as `pauseUnansweredCheckIns` in `~/.config/tasks/config.json`.

## Upgrading

- **Server:** nothing changed; no update needed.
- **Command line tool:** only the version number changed. To update it anyway:
  ```sh
  git pull && npm ci && npm run cli:install
  ```
